title: How attention alone overtook recurrent translation
subject: algorithm

brief.audience: ML practitioners who know RNNs and sequence-to-sequence models, but not the Transformer's internals
brief.focus: how replacing recurrence with self-attention made translation both better and far cheaper to train
brief.context: A recurrent network reads a sentence one word at a time, so within a sentence seven words take seven steps in a row; attention already helped, but rode on top of that recurrence.
brief.hook: Throw the recurrence away and keep only attention: a model trained for *twelve hours* comes out ahead of every published English-to-German system, ensembles included.

claims.omit: Constituency parsing is a second task with its own table; a two-minute video spends its evidence on translation, the task the method was built for.

scenes.why: Opening: the recurrent network the viewer knows, stepping through the sentence with a count of steps, then the hook said over the same sentence.

beats.say: A recurrent network reads a sentence one word at a time.
Each hidden state waits for the one before it, so within a sentence, seven words take seven steps in a row.
Attention already let the decoder look back at every word, but it rode on top of that recurrence.
Throw the recurrence away and keep only attention. A model built that way, trained for twelve hours on eight GPUs, comes out ahead of every published English-to-German system, ensembles included.

scenes.why: The viewer now knows the claim; this is the paper that makes it, by name.
scenes.title: Attention Is All You Need
scenes.subtitle: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin

beats.say: That is what the paper Attention Is All You Need sets out to show.

scenes.why: Table 1 on the sentence: recurrence reaches cat from ran in five serial steps, convolution in a stack of layers, self-attention in one direct link that every word makes at once.

beats.say: So what was the recurrence costing? In this sentence, ran needs its subject, cat, five words back.
In the recurrent network, cat travels through five steps of hidden state, none of them in parallel.
Convolutional models like ConvS2S do run in parallel, but a distant pair needs a stack of layers to meet.
Self-attention, a sentence attending to its own words, links ran to cat in one step. In the encoder, every word does this at once.
The authors argue that paths this short make distant links easier to learn.

scenes.why: The link up close, on the same sentence: ran's query against every key, divided by the square root of the key size, the scores as bars, softmax into weights that land on cat, and the weighted sum.

beats.say: Up close, each word's vector also includes a stamp of its position, since attention by itself ignores order. From it come a query, a key and a value, three learned projections.
The query of ran is dotted with every key and divided by the square root of the key size: one score per word.
Softmax turns the scores into weights, and most of the weight goes to cat.
The output for ran is the weighted sum of the values.

scenes.why: Why the paper divides by the square root of d_k: the spread of random 64-dimensional dot products, before and after, beside what that spread does to a softmax.

beats.say: Why divide before the softmax?
The model runs several attention heads side by side, each with keys of sixty-four dimensions, and random dot products of that size spread about eight times wider.
The authors suspect that pushes the softmax toward all-or-nothing, where gradients are tiny.
Dividing by eight brings the spread back to one.

scenes.title: WMT *2014* English-to-German
scenes.why: Quality against training cost is a trade-off, so each system in Table 2 is one point: the Transformer is up and to the left of everything before it.
scenes.across: estimated training cost, 10^18 FLOPs (lower is better)

beats.say: On translation, training cost, as the authors estimate it, runs along the bottom, with English-to-German BLEU up the side.
The base model, the twelve-hour one, is above and to the left of every earlier system, on the least compute.
The big model clears the best by more than two points, and sets a new single-model record on English-to-French.

cues.note: EN-FR, big model: 41.8 BLEU after 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs

scenes.why: The limit the paper names in Table 1 and Section 4: every pair gets a score, so cost grows with the square of the length, and it only beats recurrence while n < d.

beats.say: The price is paid in pairs. Every word scores every word, itself included. A thousand word pieces make a million scores, per head and per layer.

By the paper's own count, that is cheaper per layer than recurrence only while a sentence has fewer words than its vectors have dimensions, 512 here. Training runs the decoder at once too, with later words masked, but generating output is still one word at a time.

scenes.why: Recap: each takeaway beside the moment that showed it, ending on the hook's twelve hours.
scenes.title: What to keep

items.text: Any two words linked in one step
Scores divided by √d_k before the softmax
12 hours: ahead of every earlier EN-DE result

beats.say: So attention links any two words in one step, and the encoder computes every link at once.
Scaling the scores, the authors suspect, keeps the softmax trainable.
That design, trained for twelve hours, came out ahead of every published English-to-German system.
